question: Power of a lens of focal length ‘f’ is directly proportional to ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1/f**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The power of a lens (P) is defined as the reciprocal of its focal length (f) in meters.
 
• It is mathematically expressed as P=(1)/(f)
 
• The unit of power of a lens is diopter (D), where 1 D = 1 m⁻¹.
 
• A lens with a short focal length has a higher power, and a lens with a long focal length has a lower power.
 
• The power of a converging lens (convex) is positive, while the power of a diverging lens (concave) is negative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Focal Length**

 
 
• The focal length of a lens is the distance from the lens to the point where parallel rays of light converge or appear to diverge.
 
• The focal length determines the magnifying power of the lens.
 
 
 
• **Diopter**
 
 
• Diopter is a unit of measurement of the optical power of a lens.
 
• It is commonly used in the field of optometry and ophthalmology.
 
 
 
• **Lens Types**
 
 
• Convex lenses are converging lenses that bring light rays to a focus.
 
• Concave lenses are diverging lenses that spread light rays outward.
